paper.title: Huxley-Gödel Machine: Human-Level Coding Agent Development by an Approximation of the Optimal Self-Improving Machine
paper.central_claim: Clade-based metaproductivity estimation and adaptive expansion/evaluation discover better self-modifying coding agents more efficiently than DGM/SICA, with cross-task/model transfer and human-level agent-design performance.

provenance.notes: Configured agent model type sonnet; runtime states gpt-6.1-sol. No independently available model receipt or session identifier; no probing performed.

sections_read: Appendices A–F, complete proof, algorithm, details and both code listings

evidence.quote: Therefore, we decouple evaluation from expansion and treat them as separate steps.
evidence.support_explanation: Scheduler separates task evaluation from adding self-modified agent code.
New child code is retained in the archive and may become a future parent.

evidence.quote: after a maximum allowance of 800 benchmark task evaluations
evidence.support_explanation: Methods share initial ancestor and backbones but task-count matching is not dollar matching.
Search-set gains exceed DGM 53.3/27.1 and SICA 50.0/25.4; SICA context overflow is disclosed.
Authors filter overlap, leaving 207 unseen tasks; Table 3 gives 40.1 versus ancestor34.8 and SWE-agent39.6.

evidence.quote: Overall, we spent approximately $5000 USD to produce the experimental results, including all three methods.
evidence.support_explanation: Total experimental spend disclosed, but not matched per-method token/dollar costs.

evidence.quote: the Gödel Machine prover does not consume budget
evidence.support_explanation: Optimality theorem needs an oracle, repeatability, fixed final objective, free proof and equal modification cost; not a practical guarantee.

evidence.quote: this accuracy drops quickly as the number of evaluations grows
evidence.support_explanation: Authors explicitly describe asynchronous easy-task completion bias; no main search-seed intervals reported.

evidence.quote: we exclude the evaluations that are most directly related to the target
evidence.support_explanation: Correlation comparison removes root and target-containing subtree; still retrospective on different selectively observed trees.

claims.text: HGM discovers stronger agents with less allocated CPU time than DGM/SICA.
claims.setting: SWE-Verified-60 and Polyglot, common ancestor and model pair
claims.selection_vs_test: 800-evaluation search tasks reused for final best-belief reporting
claims.denominator: 60 SWE tasks; fixed Polyglot benchmark; up to800 evaluations; SICA SWE fails after360
claims.counterevidence: No independent search replication or component ablation; CPU-hours not model-call expenditure.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Reported bundled search improvement, not isolated causal proof for CMP.

claims.text: Human-level agent design and task/model generalization.
claims.baseline_control: ancestor and SWE-agent with matched GPT-5-mini; GPT-5 transfer comparison
claims.selection_vs_test: 207 disjoint filtered tasks; full300 includes93 search overlaps
claims.result: 40.1% vs34.8% ancestor and39.6% SWE-agent; GPT-5 filtered47.8 vs48.3 SWE-agent
claims.counterevidence: 0.5pp matched-baseline gain is about one task, without uncertainty; leaderboard parity not general human equivalence.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Retained code transfer beyond search tasks, not broad human-level superiority.

claims.text: CMP oracle suffices for optimal self-improvement under stated assumptions.
claims.setting: static final-agent utility, repeatable trials, known utility, free proof, unit modification budget
claims.result: Appendix A reduces oracle to state-action value for simulated accept/reject policy.
claims.counterevidence: Pooled finite-data estimator and asynchronous runtime do not satisfy an oracle premise.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Restricted oracle connection, not optimality of executed HGM.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported persistent agent code improves disjoint SWE-Lite performance versus ancestor; practical CMP/scheduler bundle beats DGM/SICA on reused search benchmarks. Evidence does not isolate an improved improver at matched dollar budget.
unresolved: No actual replication or independent whole-search seeds.
Sandbox/anchor enforcement and component causal attribution incomplete.

G.reason: Specific immediate-performance/descendant mismatch with named close methods and empirical diagnostics; independent neighbor originals unavailable.

M.reason: Reconstructable clade and individual Thompson policies address allocation bottleneck; oracle-to-estimator gap and bundle alternatives remain.

X.reason: Archive, parent/evaluation separation and later use explicit; rollback/security boundary enforcement incomplete.

E.measurement.reason: Executable benchmark outcomes and transfer denominators reported; clade proxy has retrospective selectively sampled evaluation limitations.

E.causality.reason: Common ancestor/model and DGM/SICA controls, but no CMP-only/scheduler-only/async-only or retained-component ablation.

E.holdout.reason: 207 overlapping-task-filtered held-out problems plus cross-model transfer; main search results and broad human-level claim remain limited.

E.statistics.reason: Sample sizes and negative SICA/context-bias outcomes reported; no main-result CI, significance or independent search seeds, per A2 ladder.

E.cost.reason: CPU-hours, task counts and total spend visible; no normalized per-method API/token/dollar cost or expansion-failure accounting.
